proposed_edits.section: Grasp beyond the top-down envelope: tilted orientation search, then a table relay
proposed_edits.change: Extend the Limit paragraph: 'A tilted grasp also tilts the jaw closing axis. On YAM the closing axis is tool y, which is world x at pitch 90 / yaw 0 for the tool_quat() above. tool_quat pitches about world y, so at pitch p the closing axis is (90-p) deg off horizontal and the hub hangs tilted in the jaws. Tilted insertions (pitch 60-80) stalled 11-14 mm above the seat on 5/5 seeds (yam_real gear_assembly dev 59-62, unseen 71) under four different strategies: plain descent, visual alignment, roll-90 tool, release+press. Rolling the tool 90 deg about its approach axis keeps the closing axis horizontal, but the regrasp then closed at width 0.58-0.77 (on the teeth) and still stalled. Treat an insertion pose that needs pitch < 85 as unsolved.'
proposed_edits.why: The section is graded useful for the pick, but a reader may assume the same tilted orientation works for placing or inserting. Five seeds and four strategies show it does not, and the closing-axis geometry explains why

proposed_edits.change: Add a row or warning: 'yam_real top camera, object HELD in the gripper 6-9 cm above the table: the hub-top centroid of the held gear (points within [EE_z - hold, EE_z + grasp_depth]) read -18 to -25 mm in world x relative to the EE, but the set-down ground truth was +0.6 mm (y read within 2 mm). The x bias depends on position (-24 at x 0.48, -18 at x 0.77). Never servo an in-hand offset from this view without first setting the object down and re-measuring it on the table.'
proposed_edits.why: v03 servoed on this reading and pushed the gear 2 cm off the shaft (seeds 59, 60). The calibration probe (set the gear down, re-localize it) exposed the bias

proposed_new.title: Reject 'ok' mink IK solutions by their reported position error
proposed_new.trigger: yam_real: choosing among candidate orientations (pitch/yaw search) for a precise pose such as an insertion. solve_ik(..., backend='mink') returns ok=True for any solution within 10 mm, and move_to_pose then lands up to that far away (seed 59: commanded x 0.8131, achieved 0.8059 above the shaft). IKResult.diagnostics['position_error_m'] carries the actual residual. Cost: one solve_ik per pose (~0.02 s, no ticks); arm empty or holding, it does not matter. Use a max_err that matches the precision the step needs (2 mm for a peg/bore here), and fall back to the default 10 mm only if nothing passes.
proposed_new.evidence: v01 (ok-only check) achieved 7 mm short of the above-shaft pose on 59 and 1.8 mm short on 62. v02-v06 (2 mm check) reached every chosen free-space pose within 0.2 mm on all 8 dev seeds. It removed the IK error but flipped no seed by itself: the tilted seeds failed for the reason in the blocked note
